title: Building an AI game master with a separate rules engine: Sylvia GM’s first public alpha
author: PneumaIO
selftext:
Sylvia is a free app for solo tabletop campaigns with an AI game master.



Pick a character and an adventure, describe what you do, and Sylvia runs the scene and plays the supporting cast. You can return to saved campaigns or use Builder to create and revise your own worlds, adventures and characters.



I’ve been building Sylvia with AI coding agents. One lesson from the early build was that interface expectations needed to become explicit requirements: I expected token-by-token streaming without spelling it out, but the agent could choose differently. I wrote about that here: [https://pneuma-io.dev/sylvia-gm/blog/2026-07-09-dev-log/](https://pneuma-io.dev/sylvia-gm/blog/2026-07-09-dev-log/)



That distinction between conversation and explicit behaviour is also central to the app. Sylvia calls a separate game engine for implemented rules, then narrates the result. Players can inspect the mechanical outcome alongside the story. The alpha includes SRD Lite, based on SRD 5.2.1, with 117 supported spells, plus Severed Lands adventures. Consumables aren’t included.



You connect a compatible hosted provider or an already-running local model server. Sylvia is free; inference may cost money or use subscription allowances. The code is source-available under PolyForm Noncommercial with additional permissions.



This is a public alpha. Narration can be interrupted after an action has already been saved. Keep campaign backups and read the release notes for the known issues and testing limits.



Overview: [https://pneuma-io.dev/sylvia-gm/](https://pneuma-io.dev/sylvia-gm/)



Download, setup and release notes: [https://github.com/pneuma-io/sylvia-gm/releases/tag/v0.3.0-alpha.1](https://github.com/pneuma-io/sylvia-gm/releases/tag/v0.3.0-alpha.1)



The downloads target Windows 11 x64 and require WebView2. ChatGPT account connections also need the supported Codex runtime separately.



For people building similar systems, how are you testing the boundary between an action being saved and the model describing its result?
